title: No function specification language with formal preconditions/postconditions
candidate_description: The ignition architecture lacks a formal specification language for declaring function preconditions and postconditions. External research (families 3, 7, 8) shows that refinement types, function contracts, and algebraic effects provide composable specification mechanisms. Currently ignition functions are specified in markdown with informal mathematical notation.
internal_assets_list: IGN-ASSET-001 through IGN-ASSET-005 lack formal precondition specification
No machine-checkable contract for any axiom function
No refinement type for derived functions
Theorem functions lack postcondition enforcement
Meta-functions have no formal input domain constraint language
compared_with_gap_001_to_014: DISTINCT from all existing gaps. GAP-001 concerns evidence tiers, not specification language.

four_option_analysis.option_1_new_field: Add precondition/postcondition fields to function table entries. PRO: minimal change. CON: doesn't enable machine checking.
four_option_analysis.option_2_new_object_type: Create FunctionSpec object type. PRO: clean separation. CON: adds complexity to architecture.
four_option_analysis.option_3_new_runtime_layer: Add specification checker runtime layer. PRO: enables verification. CON: heavy infrastructure.
four_option_analysis.option_4_no_change: Keep markdown specification. PRO: no disruption. CON: no machine verification possible.

counterexamples: Ψ₀ definition uses mathematical notation that resists simple type-level specification
Case studies involve historical context that cannot be preconditioned
machine_checkable_verification: Check that each function entry has precondition and postcondition fields in structured format
reasoning: While the gap is real (0 FULLTEXT_REVIEWED, insufficient for full gap promotion), the evidence supports adding specification fields rather than a new architecture layer. The gap in formal specification is important but does not meet the threshold for a new gap given 0 fulltext reviews.

title: No weight-space composition algebra for function combination
candidate_description: External research (families 1, 2, 6) shows that weight-space operations (model soups, task arithmetic, hypernetworks) enable function composition via parameter arithmetic. Ignition has no such algebra.
internal_assets_list: No composition rule for combining two ignition functions
No weight-space representation for any function
No arithmetic operation defined between functions
compared_with_gap_001_to_014: DISTINCT. No existing gap addresses function composition algebra.

four_option_analysis.option_1_new_field: Add composition_rule field. PRO: documents intent. CON: no enforcement.
four_option_analysis.option_2_new_object_type: Create CompositionRule object. PRO: structured. CON: requires interpreter.
four_option_analysis.option_3_new_runtime_layer: Add composition runtime. PRO: executable. CON: heavy.
four_option_analysis.option_4_no_change: Keep informal composition. PRO: no disruption. CON: no systematic composition.

counterexamples: Ψ₀ multiplicative structure may not compose via simple weight arithmetic
Case studies involve narrative content not amenable to algebraic composition
machine_checkable_verification: Verify composition_rule field exists and references valid operations
reasoning: 0 FULLTEXT_REVIEWED. The gap is architecturally relevant but evidence is insufficient to promote. Weight-space algebra from neural networks does not directly map to ignition's mathematical function space.

candidate_description: Families 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 all define functions with different carriers (weights, code, operators, adapters, merged models) but ignition has no framework for determining equivalence between representations.
internal_assets_list: No way to check if two markdown function definitions are equivalent
No equivalence between mathematical and computational representations
No test-based equivalence checking
No distributional equivalence metric
No formal semantic equivalence checker
compared_with_gap_001_to_014: DISTINCT. No existing gap addresses cross-representation equivalence.

four_option_analysis.option_1_new_field: Add equivalence_class field. PRO: simple. CON: no checking.
four_option_analysis.option_2_new_object_type: Create EquivalenceRelation object. PRO: structured. CON: complex.
four_option_analysis.option_3_new_runtime_layer: Add equivalence checker runtime. PRO: executable. CON: very heavy.
four_option_analysis.option_4_no_change: Manual comparison only. PRO: no effort. CON: error-prone.

candidate_description: Families 8, 9, 10 show that algebraic effect handlers, probabilistic programming, and agent skill compilation all require explicit effect tracking. Ignition functions have no effect system.
internal_assets_list: No way to declare that a function modifies state
No way to declare that a function may fail
No way to declare non-determinism
No way to track agent-side effects
compared_with_gap_001_to_014: DISTINCT. No existing gap addresses effect systems.

four_option_analysis.option_1_new_field: Add effect_signature field. PRO: lightweight. CON: declarative only.
four_option_analysis.option_2_new_object_type: Create EffectType object. PRO: structured. CON: adds complexity.
four_option_analysis.option_3_new_runtime_layer: Add effect handler runtime. PRO: executable. CON: very heavy, may not fit ignition's mathematical nature.
four_option_analysis.option_4_no_change: No effect tracking. PRO: simple. CON: cannot reason about side effects.
